drugs.name: Acetazolamide
drugs.notes: Non-weight immersion treatment; water-system correction is essential.

drugs.name: Acetic acid
drugs.indication: Supportive flock management for suspected macrorhabdiasis/dysbiosis

drugs.name: Acriflavine

drugs.name: Amantadine

drugs.name: Amantadine

drugs.name: Amantadine

drugs.name: Amantadine
drugs.indication: Adjunctive analgesia where selected by clinician

drugs.name: Amitriptyline

drugs.name: Amitriptyline
drugs.indication: Feather damaging behaviour or chronic anxiety support

drugs.name: Apomorphine

drugs.name: Aspirin

drugs.name: Aspirin

drugs.name: Betamethasone

drugs.name: Betamethasone

drugs.name: Bronopol

drugs.name: Bronopol

information.content: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitor used in fish gas bubble disease situations where water-system causes are also corrected.
High doses or inappropriate aquatic use can disturb buoyancy and cause neurological signs.
Acidifying agent used in fish dips and as low-evidence supportive flock management in some avian dysbiosis/macrorhabdus contexts.
It is corrosive/irritant in concentrated form and can be toxic to small tropical fish.
Aquatic antimicrobial/antiparasitic dye used for some external fish diseases, usually via proprietary products.
Powder is irritant and potentially mutagenic; it can harm plants and reproduction in some species.
NMDA antagonist used as adjunctive analgesia, especially chronic or neuropathic pain.
Not first-line for acute analgesia and avian analgesic efficacy is not well established.
Tricyclic antidepressant used for selected chronic anxiety and feather-damaging behaviour cases.
Start low and monitor for sedation, anticholinergic effects and extrapyramidal signs.
Dopamine agonist emetic used in ferrets when vomiting is appropriate after non-caustic toxin ingestion.
Contraindicated if caustic/corrosive material, aspiration risk or CNS depression makes emesis unsafe.
Irreversible COX inhibitor used for antiplatelet effects and sometimes mild analgesia.
Not a preferred analgesic in many exotics; GI and renal risks matter.
Non-depolarising neuromuscular blocker used during anaesthesia and sometimes for ocular examination in birds.
Requires ventilation, anaesthetic depth and recovery planning; it provides no analgesia or unconsciousness.
Immunosuppressive antimetabolite used in selected ferret inflammatory/immune-mediated disease.
CBC, platelets and liver monitoring are essential.
Potent long-acting glucocorticoid for short-term inflammatory disease or topical/ocular indications.
Avoid long-term routine use and avoid topical ocular steroid when corneal ulceration or infection is possible.
Aquatic antifungal used for fish and fish egg fungal control.
Irritant to eyes, lungs and skin; use water-system specific protocols.
Alkylating chemotherapy agent used for selected lymphoid malignancies under protocol guidance.
Cytotoxic drug requiring PPE, safe handling and CBC monitoring.
Emergency energy source used for hypoglycaemia and as part of nutrition/fluid support.
Concentrated dextrose must be given slowly/diluted appropriately and glucose must be rechecked.
Endocrine treatment for diabetes mellitus and selected hyperkalaemia contexts.
Overdose causes hypoglycaemia and hypokalaemia; serial glucose monitoring is mandatory.
Prostaglandin analogue used for NSAID-associated gastric ulcer prevention or treatment support.
Teratogenic handling risk and GI cramping/diarrhoea are important.
Volatile anaesthetic for induction and maintenance, with rapid adjustment and recovery compared with more soluble agents.
Requires calibrated vaporizer, oxygen/scavenging and close monitoring.
NSAID used for acute or chronic pain/inflammation in selected cases.
Avoid dehydration, renal compromise, GI ulcer risk and concurrent steroids/NSAIDs.
Potentiated sulphonamide antimicrobial with broad exotics use, including coccidiosis indications in some species.
Ensure hydration and monitor tear production/keratoconjunctivitis sicca risk with longer courses.
Thyroid hormone replacement used only where hypothyroidism diagnosis is confident.
Avian and reptile thyroid diagnosis is difficult; avoid use to induce moult.
ACTH analogue used diagnostically for suspected hypoadrenocorticism in ferrets.
Reserve for diagnostic testing; availability/formulation issues may apply.
Beta-2 agonist bronchodilator used in selected respiratory/emergency cases.
Monitor tachycardia, tremor and hypokalaemia; use caution in seizures, hypertension and hyperthyroidism.
Narrow-spectrum beta-lactam for susceptible infections, with parenteral rabbit use for Treponema cuniculi.
Do not use in guinea pigs, chinchillas, hamsters, gerbils or degus.
Fat-soluble vitamin used for hypovitaminosis A in selected exotic species.
Toxicity is possible; avoid combining oral and topical retinoid exposure.
Phytomenadione used for anticoagulant rodenticide toxicity or vitamin K deficiency.
Treatment duration must match toxin type and coagulation monitoring.
